_comment: The protocol, and the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for it (spec S4.4).
TypeScript interfaces and C++ parse/serialize code are BOTH generated from
this file by scripts/gen_protocol.py; the protocol ratchet regenerates and
diffs, so drift fails the build. A field that exists on one side only is a
build error, not a runtime mystery.
NAMESPACE. `lmp/*`, private, and honest about it. v1 called itself MCP,
implemented none of the handshake, and the only occurrence of `initialize`
in its transport was a parser warm-up string literal. This is not MCP and
does not claim to be (S4.4).

RunSettings._comment: 0 no execution, 1 macOS Seatbelt, 2 container (refuses until wired), 3 UNSANDBOXED on the host. The number is an identity, not a rank -- 3 is the least contained, not the most. Plan mode pins this to 0 whatever is asked for: a mode that cannot execute cannot be talked into executing by a settings field.
RunSettings.name: sandbox_tier

RunSettings._comment: false makes EVERY command execution raise a card, whatever its risk score. true keeps the risk-routed behaviour, where only the 0.35-0.85 band escalates. Named for what the operator turns on -- 'run commands without asking me' -- rather than for the harness's internal routing.
RunSettings.name: auto_approve_exec

RunSettings._comment: false makes every workspace-mutating call raise a card. Writes had no HITL path at all before: mode policy decided whether they were allowed and nothing asked about any individual one.
RunSettings.name: auto_approve_writes

RunSettings._comment: Overrides the built-in persona. The editor keeps one per mode, so 'plan' can be told to think out loud and 'agent' to be terse. Empty means the built-in, which is the only reason this can be a plain string rather than a presence flag.
RunSettings.name: system_prompt

RunSettings._comment: Commands the operator has already said yes to, newline-separated (the generator has no array type, and a newline is the one character a shell command cannot contain unescaped). An entry matches a command that equals it, or that starts with it followed by a space. A command containing shell chaining -- ; && || | ` $( > < & -- NEVER matches, because `pytest` on the allowlist must not authorise `pytest; rm -rf ~`. The irreversible-capability gate sits ABOVE this: nothing on this list can auto-approve a call that destroys data, writes outside the workspace, escalates privileges or rewrites history.
RunSettings.name: allowed_commands

lmp/cancel._comment: MUST be deliverable while the model is generating (S4.3). The reader thread parses the method field of a COMPLETE message and sets the cancel token; no substring matching on transport bytes, ever.

_comment: Talk to the agent. ONE method, two behaviours, decided by whether a run is
in flight -- because from the user's side there is only one act, 'say
something to it', and which of those two it turns out to be is the
harness's business rather than the caller's.
IN FLIGHT: steering. The text lands in the run's context at the NEXT TURN
BOUNDARY, not mid-generation. Cancel is the violent one and sets a token
mid-token-stream; steering is gentle by design, so the model finishes the
thought it is having and reads the instruction before choosing its next
move. It also marks the plan stale, which makes `plan` the only callable
tool on the following turn -- so an instruction cannot be received and
then quietly ignored (S9.2: mechanism, not a sentence asking it to listen).
IDLE: a follow-up. The same ContextStore, the same loaded weights, one more
user turn. `started_run` says which happened, and `run_id` names the run
the text went to either way.

lmp/approval_request._comment: The command verbatim, when there is one. `preview` truncates each argument at 120 characters for display, so it is the wrong thing to remember an allowlist rule from -- a truncated rule would either never match again or, worse, match something shorter than what was approved.
lmp/approval_request.name: command

lmp/approval_request._comment: Whether this call carries a capability that cannot be undone. Computed by the loop and sent, rather than re-derived in the view from the chips, so the UI and the gate cannot disagree about which calls are unwaivable.
lmp/approval_request.name: irreversible

lmp/run_end._comment: Checklist items still open when the run ended. `completed` is an EVIDENTIAL verdict -- a recorded deliverable plus a falsifiable passing verification of the declared contract -- so it no longer waits on the model agreeing that it is done. This field reports the disagreement instead of hiding it: completed=true with unfinished_items>0 means the evidence says the mission is met and the model's own list says otherwise, and a human should look.
lmp/run_end.name: unfinished_items
